In Chapter 11, we saw a generic framework for work queue processing, as well as a number of example applications of simple work queue processing. Work queues are great for enabling individual transformations of one input to one output. However, there are a number of batch applications where you want to perform more than a single action, or you may need to generate multiple different outputs from a single data input. In these cases, you start to link work queues together so that the output of one work queue becomes the input to one or more other work queues, and so on. This forms a series of processing steps that respond to events, with the events being the completion of the preceding step in the work queue that came before it.

在第 11 章中，我们看到了一个用于工作队列处理的通用框架，以及若干简单工作队列处理的示例应用。工作队列非常适合实现“一个输入变换为一个输出”这种单次变换。然而，有许多批处理应用，你想要执行的不只是单个动作，或者你需要从单个数据输入生成多个不同的输出。在这些情况下，你就开始把工作队列链接起来，让一个工作队列的输出成为另一个或多个工作队列的输入，依此类推。这就形成了一系列响应事件的处理步骤，这里的事件就是“前一个工作队列中前一步骤的完成”。

These sort of event-driven processing systems are often called workflow systems, since there is a flow of work through a directed, acyclic graph that describes the various stages and their coordination. A basic illustration of such a system is shown in Figure 12-1.

这类事件驱动的处理系统通常被称为工作流（workflow）系统，因为工作是流经一个有向无环图的，该图描述了各个阶段及其协作关系。图 12-1 给出了这种系统的一个基本示意图。

The most straightforward application of this type of system simply chains the output of one queue to the input of the next queue. But as systems become more complicated, there are a series of different patterns that emerge for linking a series of work queues together. Understanding and designing in terms of these patterns is important for comprehending how the system is working. The operation of an event-driven batch processor is similar to event-driven FaaS. Consequently, without an overall blueprint for how the different event queues relate to each other, it can be hard to fully understand how the system is operating. Furthermore, though the initial design of a work queue can be straightforward, correctly handling errors and other unexpected conditions rapidly makes a simple work queue much more complicated.

这类系统最直接的应用，就是把一个队列的输出简单链接到下一个队列的输入。但随着系统变得更复杂，会涌现出一系列不同的模式，用于把多个工作队列链接在一起。从这些模式的角度去理解和设计，对于把握系统如何运转非常重要。事件驱动批处理器的运行方式类似于事件驱动的 FaaS（函数即服务）。因此，如果没有一份描述各个事件队列如何相互关联的整体蓝图，就很难完全理解系统是如何运作的。此外，虽然工作队列的初始设计可能很直接，但要正确处理错误和其他意外情况，很快就会让一个简单的工作队列变得复杂得多。

Patterns of Event-Driven Processing事件驱动处理的模式

Beyond the simple work queue described in Chapter 11, there are a number of patterns for linking work queues together. The simplest pattern—one where the output of a single queue becomes the input to a second queue—is straightforward enough that we won't cover it here. We will describe patterns that involve the coordination of multiple different queues or the modification of the output of one or more work queues.

除了第 11 章描述的简单工作队列之外，还有若干用于把工作队列链接在一起的模式。最简单的那种模式——单个队列的输出成为第二个队列的输入——足够直白，我们这里不再赘述。我们要描述的是那些涉及多个不同队列之间协作、或对一个或多个工作队列的输出进行修改的模式。

Copier复制器（Copier）

The first pattern for coordinating work queues is a copier. The job of a copier is to take a single stream of work items and duplicate it out into two or more identical streams. This pattern is useful when there are multiple different pieces of work to be done on the same work item. An example of this might be rendering a video. When rendering a video, there are a variety of different formats that are useful, depending on where the video is intended to be shown. There might be a 4K high-resolution

协调工作队列的第一个模式是复制器（copier）。复制器的工作是：拿一串工作项，把它复制成两个或多个相同的流。当同一个工作项上需要完成多种不同工作时，这个模式就很有用。一个例子是视频渲染。渲染视频时，根据视频打算在哪里播放，会有多种不同格式都很有用。可能会有一个 4K 高分辨率

— PDF 第 151 页 —

format for playing off of a hard drive, a 1080-pixel rendering for digital streaming, a low-resolution format for streaming to mobile users on slow networks, and an animated GIF thumbnail for displaying in a movie-picking user interface. All of these work items can be modeled as separate work queues for each render, but the input to each work item is identical. An illustration of the copier pattern applied to transcoding is shown in Figure 12-2.

格式用于从硬盘播放，一个 1080 像素的渲染用于数字流媒体，一个低分辨率格式用于向慢网络上的移动用户串流，还有一个动画 GIF 缩略图用于在选片用户界面中展示。所有这些工作项都可以建模成各自独立的工作队列、每种渲染一个，但每个工作项的输入是相同的。图 12-2 展示了复制器模式应用于转码的情形。

The copy pattern can also be used to trade additional computational power for increased reliability or performance. Imagine that you have a worker processing work that usually takes one second to run, but occasionally takes one minute (60x slowdown). If you process every work item twice and take whichever result completes first, you are much less likely to be impacted by this slowdown. Similarly, if your worker crashes 1% of the time, you can go from a two-nines (99% reliable) system to a four-nines (99.99% reliable) simply by processing every item twice. Obviously, in both cases, doing the engineering work to improve the system is a better long-term solution. But sometimes as a temporary workaround, or in situations where the engineering work isn't possible, it's useful to be able to just throw resources at the problem.

复制模式也可以用来“用额外的算力换取更高的可靠性或性能”。设想你有一个 worker 处理工作，通常只要一秒，但偶尔会花一分钟（慢了 60 倍）。如果你把每个工作项处理两遍、取最先完成的那个结果，你受这种变慢影响的概率就大大降低。类似地，如果你的 worker 有 1% 的概率崩溃，那么只要把每个项处理两遍，你就能从一个两个九（99% 可靠）的系统提升到四个九（99.99% 可靠）。显然，在这两种情况下，真正做工程改进才是更长远的解决方案。但有时作为临时的权宜之计，或者在工程改进无法实现的情况下，能够直接向问题堆资源，是很有用的。

Filter过滤器（Filter）

The second pattern for event-driven batch processing is a filter. The role of a filter is to reduce a stream of work items to a smaller stream of work items by filtering out work items that don't meet particular criteria. As an example of this, consider setting up a batch workflow that handles new users signing up for a service. Some set of those users will have ticked the checkbox that indicates that they wish to be contacted via email for promotions and other information. In such a workflow, you can filter

事件驱动批处理的第二个模式是过滤器（filter）。过滤器的作用是：通过筛掉不满足特定条件的工作项，把一串工作项缩减为更小的一串。举个例子，设想你搭建一个批处理工作流，处理注册某项服务的新用户。这些用户中有一部分勾选了复选框，表示他们希望通过邮件收到促销和其他信息。在这样的工作流中，你可以过滤

— PDF 第 152 页 —

the set of newly signed-up users to only be those who have explicitly opted into being contacted.

这批新注册用户，只保留那些明确选择愿意被联系的用户。

Ideally you would compose a filter work queue source as an ambassador that wraps up an existing work queue source. The original source container provides the complete list of items to be worked on, and the filter container then adjusts that list based on the filter criteria and only returns those filtered results to the work queue infrastructure. An illustration of this use of the adapter pattern is shown in Figure 12-3.

理想情况下，你会把一个过滤器工作队列源组合成一个 ambassador，包装在一个已有工作队列源之外。原始源容器提供待处理条目的完整列表，过滤器容器再根据过滤条件调整这个列表，只把过滤后的结果返回给工作队列基础设施。图 12-3 展示了这种适配器模式的用法。

Splitter拆分器（Splitter）

Sometimes you don't want to just filter things out by dropping them on the floor, but rather you have two different kinds of input present in your set of work items, and you want to divide them into two separate work queues without dropping any of them. For this task, you want to use a splitter. The role of a splitter is to evaluate some criteria—just like a filter—but instead of eliminating input, the splitter sends different inputs to different queues based on that criteria.

有时你不想只是把东西丢掉过滤掉，而是你的工作项集合里存在两种不同的输入，你想把它们划分到两个独立的工作队列里，而不丢掉其中任何一个。这时你要使用拆分器（splitter）。拆分器的作用是评估某些条件——就像过滤器一样——但它不是丢弃输入，而是根据这些条件把不同的输入发送到不同的队列。

An example of an application of the splitter pattern is processing online orders where people can receive shipping notifications either by email or text message. Given a work queue of items that have been shipped, the splitter divides it into two different queues: one that is responsible for sending emails and another devoted to sending text messages. A splitter can also be a copier if it sends the same output to multiple queues, such as when a user selects both text messages and email notifications in the previous example. It is interesting to note that a splitter can actually also be implemented by a copier and two different filters. But the splitter pattern is a more

拆分器模式的一个应用例子是处理在线订单，用户可以通过邮件或短信接收发货通知。给定一个“已发货项”的工作队列，拆分器把它分成两个不同队列：一个负责发邮件，另一个专门发短信。如果拆分器把同一份输出发送到多个队列，它也可以同时是一个复制器——比如在前一个例子中用户同时选择了短信和邮件通知。值得注意的是，拆分器其实也可以用一个复制器加两个不同的过滤器来实现。但拆分器模式是一种更

— PDF 第 153 页 —

compact representation that captures the job of the splitter more succinctly. This is a little like the fact that an XOR (exclusive or) logic gate can actually be implemented with OR/NOT/AND gates, but it is convenient to think of it as an XOR. An example of using the splitter pattern to send shipping notifications to users is shown in Figure 12-4.

紧凑的表示，能更简洁地刻画拆分器的职责。这有点像：一个 XOR（异或）门其实可以用 OR/NOT/AND 门搭出来，但把它当作一个 XOR 来思考要方便得多。图 12-4 展示了使用拆分器模式向用户发送发货通知的例子。

Sharder分片器（Sharder）

A slightly more generic form of splitter is a sharder. Much like the sharded server that we saw in earlier chapters, the role of a sharder in a workflow is to divide up a single queue into an evenly divided collection of work items based upon some sort of sharding function. There are several different reasons why you might consider sharding your workflow. One of the first is for reliability. If you shard your work queue, then the failure of a single workflow due to a bad update, infrastructure failure, or other problem only affects a fraction of your service.

拆分器的一种稍微更通用的形式是分片器（sharder）。很像我们在前面章节看到的分片服务器，分片器在工作流中的作用是：根据某种分片函数，把单个队列划分成一组均匀分布的工作项。你可能会考虑对工作流做分片，原因有好几个。首要原因之一是可靠性。如果你把工作队列分片，那么由于一次糟糕的更新、基础设施故障或其他问题导致单个工作流失败时，它只会影响你服务的一小部分。

For example, imagine that you push a bad update to your worker container, which causes your workers to crash and your queue to stop processing work items. If you only have a single work queue that is processing items, then you will have a complete outage for your service with all users affected. If, instead, you have sharded your work queue into four different shards, you have the opportunity to do a staged rollout of your new worker container. Assuming you catch the failure in the first phase of the staged rollout, sharding your queue into four different shards means that only one-quarter of your users would be affected.

例如，设想你给 worker 容器推了一个糟糕的更新，导致 worker 崩溃、队列停止处理工作项。如果你只有一个工作队列在处理条目，那么你的服务会完全中断，所有用户都受影响。反过来，如果你已经把工作队列分成了四个不同的分片，你就有机会对新 worker 容器做分阶段发布。假设你在分阶段发布的第一阶段就发现了故障，那么把队列分成四个分片意味着只有四分之一的用户会受到影响。

— PDF 第 154 页 —

An additional reason to shard your work queue is to more evenly distribute work across different resources. If you don't really care which region or data center is used to process a particular set of work items, you can use a sharder to evenly spread work across multiple data centers to even out utilization of all data centers/regions. As with updates, spreading your work queue across multiple failure regions also has the benefit of providing reliability against data center or region failures. An illustration of a sharded queue when everything is working correctly is shown in Figure 12-5.

对工作队列分片的另一个原因，是把工作更均匀地分配到不同资源上。如果你并不在意由哪个区域或数据中心来处理某一组工作项，就可以用分片器把工作均匀地分散到多个数据中心，从而均衡所有数据中心/区域的利用率。和发布更新一样，把工作队列分散到多个故障域，还有一个好处：在数据中心或区域故障时提供可靠性。图 12-5 展示了一切正常运行时分片队列的示意图。

When the number of healthy shards is reduced due to failures, the sharding algorithm dynamically adjusts to send work to the remaining healthy work queues, even if only a single queue remains. This is illustrated in Figure 12-6.

当健康分片的数量因故障而减少时，分片算法会动态调整，把工作发送给剩余的健康工作队列，哪怕只剩下一个队列。如图 12-6 所示。

— PDF 第 155 页 —

Merger合并器（Merger）

The last pattern for event-driven or workflow batch systems is a merger. A merger is the opposite of a copier; the job of a merger is to take two different work queues and turn them into a single work queue. Suppose, for example, that you have a large number of different source repositories all adding new commits at the same time. You want to take each of these commits and perform a build-and-test for it. It is not scalable to create a separate build infrastructure for each source repository. We can model each of the different source repositories as a separate work queue source that provides a set of commits. We can transform all of these different work queue inputs into a single merged set of inputs using a merger adapter. This merged stream of commits is then the single source to the build system that performs the actual build. The merger is another great example of the adapter pattern, though in this case, the adapter is actually adapting multiple running source containers into a single merged source.

事件驱动或工作流批处理系统的最后一个模式是合并器（merger）。合并器与复制器相反；合并器的工作是把两个不同的工作队列合并成单个工作队列。举个例子，假设你有大量不同的源代码仓库，它们都在同时提交新的 commit。你想对每个 commit 做一次构建加测试。为每个源代码仓库都创建一套独立的构建基础设施是不可扩展的。我们可以把每个不同的源代码仓库建模成一个独立的工作队列源，提供一批 commit。然后用一个合并器适配器，把所有这些不同的工作队列输入变换成单一合并后的输入集合。这条合并后的 commit 流，就是执行实际构建的构建系统的唯一来源。合并器是适配器模式的又一个绝佳例子，只不过这一次，适配器是把多个正在运行的源容器适配成单一合并后的源。

— PDF 第 156 页 —

This multiadapter pattern is shown in Figure 12-7.

这种多适配器模式如图 12-7 所示。

Hands On: Building an Event-Driven Flow for New User Signup动手实践：为新用户注册构建一个事件驱动流

A concrete example of a workflow helps show how these patterns can be put together to form a complete operating system. The problem this example will consider is a new user signup flow.

一个具体的工作流例子，有助于展示这些模式如何被组合起来、形成一个完整运行的系统。这个例子要考虑的问题是新用户注册流程。

Imagine that our user acquisition funnel has two stages. The first is user verification. After a new user signs up, the user then has to receive an email notification to validate their email. Once the user validates their email, they are sent a confirmation email. Then they are optionally registered for email, text message, both, or neither for notifications.

设想我们的用户获取漏斗有两个阶段。第一阶段是用户验证。新用户注册之后，必须收到一封邮件通知来验证自己的邮箱。用户一旦验证了邮箱，就会收到一封确认邮件。然后，他们可以选择是否注册邮件、短信、两者都要、或两者都不要的通知方式。

— PDF 第 157 页 —

The first step in the event-driven workflow is the generation of the verification email. To achieve this reliably, we will use the shard pattern to shard users across multiple different geographic failure zones. This ensures that we will continue to process new user signups, even in the presence of partial failures. Each work queue shard sends a verification email to the end user. At this point, this substage of the workflow is complete. This first stage of the flow is illustrated in Figure 12-8.

这个事件驱动工作流的第一步是生成验证邮件。为了可靠地做到这一点，我们将使用分片模式，把用户分片到多个不同的地理故障域。这确保即使出现部分故障，我们仍能继续处理新用户注册。每个工作队列分片都向终端用户发送一封验证邮件。到这一步，工作流的这个子阶段就完成了。流程的第一阶段如图 12-8 所示。

The workflow begins again when we receive a verification email from the end user. These emails become new events in a separate (but clearly related) workflow that sends welcome emails and sets up notifications. The first stage of this workflow is an example of the copier pattern, where the user is copied into two work queues. The first work queue is responsible for sending the welcome email, and the second work queue is responsible for setting up user notifications.

当我们收到终端用户发来的验证邮件时，工作流再次启动。这些邮件成为另一个独立（但明显相关）工作流中的新事件，那个工作流负责发送欢迎邮件并设置通知。这个工作流的第一阶段是复制器模式的一个例子：用户被复制进两个工作队列。第一个工作队列负责发送欢迎邮件，第二个工作队列负责设置用户通知。

Once the work items have been duplicated between the queues, the email-sending queue simply takes care of sending an email message, and the workflow exits. But remember that because of the use of the copier pattern, there is still an additional copy of the event active in our workflow. This copier triggers an additional work queue to handle notification settings. This work queue feeds into an example of the filter pattern, which splits the work queue into separate email and text message notification queues. These specific queues register the user for email, text, or both notifications.

一旦工作项在两个队列之间被复制完毕，发邮件的队列就只负责发出一封邮件，然后工作流退出。但请记住，由于使用了复制器模式，我们的工作流中仍有一份额外的事件副本处于活动状态。这个复制器会触发另一个工作队列来处理通知设置。这个工作队列又接入一个过滤器模式的例子，后者把工作队列拆成独立的邮件通知队列和短信通知队列。这些具体的队列把用户注册为邮件、短信、或两者兼有的通知方式。

The remainder of this workflow is shown in Figure 12-9.

这个工作流的其余部分如图 12-9 所示。

Publisher/Subscriber Infrastructure发布/订阅基础设施

We have seen a variety of abstract patterns for linking together different event-driven batch processing patterns. But when it comes time to actually build such a system, we need to figure out how to manage the stream of data that passes through the event-driven workflow. The simplest thing to do would be to simply write each element in the work queue to a particular directory on a local filesystem, and then have each stage monitor that directory for input. But of course doing this with a local filesystem limits our workflow to operating on a single node. We can introduce a network filesystem to distribute files to multiple nodes, but this introduces increasing complexity both in our code and in the deployment of the batch workflow.

我们已经看到了各种把不同事件驱动批处理模式链接在一起的抽象模式。但当真要构建这样一个系统时，我们需要想清楚如何管理流经事件驱动工作流的数据流。最简单的做法，就是把工作队列中的每个元素写到本地文件系统的某个目录里，然后让每个阶段监视该目录以获取输入。但显然，用本地文件系统这样做，会把我们的工作流限制在单个节点上运行。我们可以引入网络文件系统来把文件分发到多个节点，但这会在代码和批处理工作流的部署上都引入越来越高的复杂度。

Instead, a popular approach to building a workflow like this is to use a publisher/subscriber (pub/sub) API or service. A pub/sub API allows a user to define a collection of queues (sometimes called topics). One or more publishers publishes messages to these queues. Likewise, one or more subscribers is listening to these queues for new messages. When a message is published, it is reliably stored by the queue and subsequently delivered to subscribers in a reliable manner.

相反，构建这类工作流的一种流行做法，是使用发布/订阅（pub/sub）API 或服务。pub/sub API 允许用户定义一组队列（有时称为主题 topic）。一个或多个发布者向这些队列发布消息。同样，一个或多个订阅者监听这些队列以获取新消息。当一条消息被发布时，它会被队列可靠地存储，随后以可靠的方式投递给订阅者。

— PDF 第 159 页 —

At this point, most public clouds feature a pub/sub API such as Azure's EventGrid or Amazon's Simple Queue Service. Additionally, the open source Kafka project provides a very popular pub/sub implementation that you can run on your own hardware as well as on cloud virtual machines. For the remainder of this overview of pub/sub APIs, we'll use Kafka for our examples, but they are relatively simple to port to alternate pub/sub APIs.

如今，大多数公有云都提供 pub/sub API，例如 Azure 的 EventGrid 或 Amazon 的 Simple Queue Service。此外，开源的 Kafka 项目提供了一个非常流行的 pub/sub 实现，你既可以在自己的硬件上运行，也可以在云虚拟机上运行。在本次 pub/sub API 概述的剩余部分中，我们将以 Kafka 为例，但这些示例相对容易移植到其他 pub/sub API。

Hands On: Deploying Kafka动手实践：部署 Kafka

There are obviously many ways to deploy Kafka, and one of the easiest ways is to run it as a container using a Kubernetes cluster and the Helm package manager. Helm is a package manager for Kubernetes that makes it easy to deploy and manage prepackaged off-the-shelf applications like Kafka. If you don't already have the helm command-line tool installed, you can install it from the Helm website.

部署 Kafka 的方式显然有很多种，最简单的方式之一是用 Kubernetes 集群加上 Helm 包管理器，把它作为容器运行。Helm 是 Kubernetes 的包管理器，让部署和管理像 Kafka 这样预打包的现成应用变得很容易。如果你还没有安装 helm 命令行工具，可以从 Helm 网站安装。

Once the helm tool is on your machine, you need to initialize it. Initializing Helm deploys a cluster-side component named tiller to your cluster and installs some templates to your local filesystem:

helm 工具装到机器上之后，你需要初始化它。初始化 Helm 会把一个名为 tiller 的集群侧组件部署到你的集群中，并把一些模板安装到你的本地文件系统：

helm init

Now that Helm is initialized, you can install Kafka using this command:

Helm 初始化完成后，你可以用下面这条命令安装 Kafka：

helm repo add incubator http://storage.googleapis.com/kubernetes-charts-incubator
helm install --name kafka-service incubator/kafka

Helm templates have different levels of production hardening and support. stable templates are the most strictly vetted and supported, whereas incubator templates like Kafka are more experimental and have less production mileage. Regardless, incubator templates are useful for quick proof of concepts as well as a place to start from when implementing a production deployment of a Kubernetes-based service.

Helm 模板在生产环境的加固程度和支持力度上有所不同。stable 模板经过最严格的审查和支持，而像 Kafka 这样的 incubator 模板则更偏实验性、在生产环境中的历练较少。尽管如此，incubator 模板对于快速的概念验证很有用，也是在基于 Kubernetes 的服务上实现生产部署时一个不错的起点。

Once you have Kafka up and running, you can create a topic to publish to. Generally in batch processing, you're going to use a topic to represent the output of one module in your workflow. This output is likely to be the input for another module in the workflow.

Kafka 跑起来之后，你就可以创建一个用于发布的 topic。一般在批处理中，你会用一个 topic 来表示工作流中某个模块的输出。这个输出很可能就是工作流中另一个模块的输入。

For example, if you are using the Sharder pattern described previously, you would have a topic for each of the output shards. If you called your output Photos and you chose to have three shards, then you would have three topics: Photos-1, Photos-2, and Photos-3. Your sharder module would output messages to the appropriate topic after applying the sharding function.

例如，如果你正在使用前面描述的分片器模式，那么每个输出分片都会有一个 topic。如果你把输出命名为 Photos，并选择分成三个分片，那么你就会有三个 topic：Photos-1、Photos-2 和 Photos-3。你的分片器模块在应用分片函数之后，会把消息输出到相应的 topic。

— PDF 第 160 页 —

Here's how you create a topic. First, create a container in the cluster so that you can access Kafka:

下面是创建 topic 的方法。首先，在集群中创建一个容器，以便访问 Kafka：

for x in 0 1 2; do
  kubectl run kafka --image=solsson/kafka:0.11.0.0 --rm --attach --command -- \
    ./bin/kafka-topics.sh --create --zookeeper kafka-service-zookeeper:2181 \
      --replication-factor 3 --partitions 10 --topic photos-$x
done

Note that there are two interesting parameters in addition to the topic name and the ZooKeeper service. They are --replication-factor and --partitions. The replication factor is how many different machines messages in the topic will be replicated to. This is the redundancy that is available in case things crash. A value of 3 or 5 is recommended. The second parameter is the number of partitions for the topic. The number of partitions represents the maximum distribution of the topic onto multiple machines for purposes of load balancing. In this case, since there are 10 partitions, there can be at most 10 different replicas of the topic for load balancing.

注意，除了 topic 名称和 ZooKeeper 服务之外，还有两个值得关注的参数：--replication-factor 和 --partitions。replication factor（副本因子）是指该 topic 中的消息会被复制到多少台不同的机器上。这就是在出故障时可用的冗余。建议取 3 或 5。第二个参数是 topic 的分区数。分区数表示为了负载均衡，该 topic 最多能分布到多少台机器上。在本例中，由于有 10 个分区，该 topic 最多可以有 10 个不同副本用于负载均衡。

Now that we have created a topic, we can send messages to that topic:

创建好 topic 之后，我们就可以向它发送消息：

kubectl run kafka-producer --image=solsson/kafka:0.11.0.0 --rm -it --command -- \
    ./bin/kafka-console-producer.sh --broker-list kafka-service-kafka:9092 \
    --topic photos-1

Once that command is up and connected, you should see the Kafka prompt, and you can then send messages to the topic(s). To receive messages, you can run:

该命令启动并连接之后，你应该会看到 Kafka 提示符，然后就可以向 topic 发送消息了。要接收消息，可以运行：

kubectl run kafka-consumer --image=solsson/kafka:0.11.0.0 --rm -it --command -- \
    ./bin/kafka-console-consumer.sh --bootstrap-server kafka-service-kafka:9092\
    --topic photos-1 \
        --from-beginning

Of course, running these command lines only gives you a taste of how to communicate via Kafka messages. To build a real-world event-driven batch processing system, you would likely use a proper programming language and Kafka SDK to access the service. But on the other hand, never underestimate the power of a good bash script!

当然，运行这些命令行只是让你尝一尝如何通过 Kafka 消息通信。要构建一个真实世界的事件驱动批处理系统，你很可能会用一门正经的编程语言和 Kafka SDK 来访问该服务。但另一方面，永远不要低估一个好的 bash 脚本的威力！

This section has shown how installing Kafka into your Kubernetes cluster can dramatically simplify the task of building a work queue-based system.

本节展示了：把 Kafka 安装到你的 Kubernetes 集群中，如何能极大地简化构建基于工作队列的系统这一任务。

Resiliency and Performance in Work Queues工作队列中的弹性与性能

So far in this chapter, we have designed workflows to optimize the design of the work queue to match the problem being addressed by the work queue. This is an important part of engineering. The clearer the design of the system matches the task, the easier it is to understand, update, and extend. However, an additional critical part of engineering is anticipating and designing systems for both the performance and reliability requirements of the users.

本章到目前为止，我们设计工作流，是为了优化工作队列的设计，使之与工作队列要解决的问题相匹配。这是工程中重要的一部分。系统设计与任务匹配得越清晰，就越容易理解、更新和扩展。然而，工程中另一个关键部分，是预见用户对性能和可靠性的需求，并据此设计系统。

— PDF 第 161 页 —

So far, in all of the designs we have assumed that all of the work in the system is roughly identical and each piece of work is equally reliable. Unfortunately, in the real world, neither one of these assumptions is typically true. Unless your system is very, very unusual, it contains a mix of different work. Different videos, different emails, different builds—work queues are constantly dealing with similar but different individual pieces of work.

到目前为止，在所有这些设计中，我们都假设系统中的所有工作大致相同，且每一项工作的可靠性都一样。不幸的是，在现实世界中，这两个假设通常都不成立。除非你的系统非常非常特殊，否则它总是混杂着不同的工作：不同的视频、不同的邮件、不同的构建——工作队列一直在处理相似但各不相同的单项工作。

Work Stealing工作窃取（Work Stealing）

The net result of this is that some pieces of work take longer than other pieces of work. Sometimes this is inherent (that movie is just larger), but often it is because of design decisions in our code which are better or worse fits for a specific work item. We may have optimized our code for lots of files and few directories, and the work item might be the opposite: deep directory trees with relatively few files. Oftentimes the latency of individual work items might not matter; if they generally land on different queues via something like sharding, the overall average times generally work out. But unfortunately, sometimes this average performance doesn't work out, and all of the slow items end up on one queue. When this happens, the inputs to the queue pile up and latency increases, much like a slow checkout lane in a grocery store. Just like in the grocery store, the best option is to move from the slow lane to a lane with a shorter line. This algorithm is called “work stealing.”

其最终结果是：有些工作项比其他工作项耗时更长。有时这是固有的（那部电影就是更大），但更多时候是因为我们代码中的设计决策，对某个特定工作项适配得好或坏。我们可能把代码优化成“文件多、目录少”的情形，而某个工作项可能恰好相反：目录树很深、文件相对较少。单个工作项的延迟往往并不重要；如果它们通过分片之类的机制大体落到不同队列上，总体平均时间通常能算得过来。但不幸的是，有时这种平均表现并不奏效，所有慢的项最终都挤到了一个队列上。这时队列的输入开始堆积、延迟上升，就像杂货店里一条结账很慢的通道。就像在杂货店里一样，最好的办法是从慢通道换到队伍更短的通道。这种算法叫做“工作窃取”。

The basic algorithm for work stealing says that for any worker, as long as that worker has work on their queue, the work on the queue is performed as you would expect. When there is no work on a worker's queue, instead of sleeping until more work arrives, the worker takes work off of the back of the longest queue of any other worker. In this way, the maximum length of any work queue is kept to a minimum since workers with shorter work queues remove work from workers with longer queues. Work is taken from the back of the queue because that removal can be done safely without worrying about whether the work may be performed by multiple workers.

工作窃取的基本算法是：对任何一个 worker，只要它自己队列上还有工作，就按你预期的方式处理队列上的工作。当某个 worker 的队列上没有工作时，它不会睡大觉等待更多工作到来，而是从其他 worker 最长队列的尾部取走工作。这样一来，任何工作队列的最大长度都被压到最小，因为队列短的 worker 会从队列长的 worker 那里取走工作。之所以从队列尾部取工作，是因为这样取走是安全的，不必担心同一份工作会被多个 worker 同时处理。

Errors, Priority, and Retry错误、优先级与重试

The other problems that can occur in a work queue system come when there are errors processing the work itself. The first problem that can happen is if your worker crashes in the middle of processing the work. In the worst case, the work that was being removed from the queue is lost. Fortunately, most queue systems have semantics where the message being processed is initially removed from the queue for processing. This initial removal hides the message from other workers, but it doesn't actually remove it from the queue. When the work has been processed, a second “completed” message is sent to the queue, which permanently removes the work from the queue. Typically a message queue has a timeout after which, if the work has not

工作队列系统中可能出现的另一类问题，出现在处理工作本身出错时。第一个可能发生的问题是：worker 在处理工作的中途崩溃。在最坏情况下，正从队列中取出处理的那份工作就丢失了。幸运的是，大多数队列系统都有这样的语义：正在处理的消息一开始会从队列中“移除”出来以供处理。这种初始的移除把消息对其他 worker 隐藏起来，但并没有真正把它从队列中删掉。当工作处理完成后，会向队列发送第二条“已完成”消息，把该工作永久地从队列中移除。通常消息队列有一个超时时间，超过之后，如果工作还没有

— PDF 第 162 页 —

been “completed,” the work item is returned to the head of the queue for other workers to pick it up.

被“完成”，该工作项就会被退回到队列头部，供其他 worker 拾取。

Unfortunately, recovering from this error results in an additional complication. What if the first worker is merely running slowly, not crashed? Now we have two workers processing the same work item. The easiest way to deal with this situation is to make each work item idempotent. That way the additional processing is wasted computation, but it does not cause any additional errors. If it isn't possible to make your work idempotent, there are various distributed locking methods discussed in previous chapters that can be used. The important takeaway is that when writing a worker, you must assume that multiple workers could be operating on the same work item.

不幸的是，从这种错误中恢复会带来额外的复杂度。如果第一个 worker 只是跑得慢、并没有崩溃呢？这时就有两个 worker 在处理同一个工作项了。处理这种情况最简单的办法，是让每个工作项都是幂等的。这样一来，重复的处理只是浪费计算，但不会引发任何额外错误。如果无法让工作幂等，前面章节讨论过的各种分布式锁方法也可以使用。重要的启示是：写 worker 时，你必须假设可能有多个 worker 正在处理同一个工作项。

Assuming idempotent work, we're now safe from workers crashing, right? Sadly, it's not that easy. Imagine if the crashing worker is not due to random bugs in the worker's code, but something about the work item itself. Suppose there is a “poison” work item which crashes a worker 100% of the time. In such a situation, where one worker is recovering from the crash, the poison work is picked up by another worker, which itself crashes, causing another worker to pick up the poison and so on and so forth until all of your workers are crashing. Even if you are lucky and your workers recover quickly, poison work can cause you to lose a significant percentage of your worker capacity and slow down your work queue significantly.

假设工作是幂等的，我们现在就对 worker 崩溃免疫了，对吧？可惜事情没那么简单。设想 worker 崩溃不是因为 worker 代码里的随机 bug，而是工作项本身有问题。假设有一个“毒丸”工作项，它 100% 会让 worker 崩溃。在这种情况下，当一个 worker 从崩溃中恢复时，这份毒丸工作又被另一个 worker 拾取，而那个 worker 自己也崩溃，于是又一个 worker 拾取毒丸，如此循环往复，直到你所有的 worker 都在崩溃。即使你运气好、worker 恢复得快，毒丸工作也会让你损失相当大比例的 worker 产能，并显著拖慢工作队列。

Much as with error handling, the first solution to poison work is to keep track of the number of times that a particular piece of work has been removed from the message queue. We can then use exponential backoff to increase the timeout for the poison message larger and larger until we remove it from processing entirely. Generally, exponential backoff will solve the problem of poison work.

和错误处理很像，解决毒丸工作的第一个办法是：跟踪某份特定工作从消息队列中被取出的次数。然后我们可以用指数退避（exponential backoff）把毒丸消息的超时时间越调越大，直到把它彻底移出处理流程为止。通常，指数退避就能解决毒丸工作的问题。

Unfortunately, requeuing work for processing introduces additional problems. To understand why, consider the case where workers are crashing for reasons unrelated to the work. Perhaps a downstream dependency is returning bad data and causing the crash. In this situation, the work queue effectively stalls, and more and more work piles up in the queue. Since no workers can make progress, even work stealing described previously won't help. Suppose the situation resolves itself and the workers can start making progress, like a traffic jam long after an accident; all of the work that has piled up in the queue means that new requests are still experiencing significant latency. This is often made especially bad in user-facing situations where the old work items are often no longer relevant, but the new work has value if it can be completed in time.

不幸的是，把工作重新入队等待处理会引入额外问题。要理解原因，请考虑这样一种情况：worker 崩溃的原因与工作本身无关。也许是某个下游依赖返回了坏数据、从而导致崩溃。在这种情况下，工作队列实际上停滞了，队列里堆积的工作越来越多。既然没有任何 worker 能取得进展，连前面描述的工作窃取也无济于事。假设局面自行恢复、worker 开始取得进展——就像事故发生很久之后的交通堵塞——队列里堆积的所有工作意味着新请求仍然要承受显著的延迟。在面向用户的场景下，这一点往往尤其糟糕：旧的工作项常常已经不再重要，但新的工作如果能及时完成是有价值的。

To address this problem of a backlog, it is often useful to actually have two queues of work items. The first queue is used for all work items which have never had an attempt made at processing. The second queue is the “retry” queue, which is used for any message which has had at least one (unsuccessful) attempt at processing. Using this dual queue approach, in the above situation, there will be a lot of work piled up

为了解决积压问题，实际上设置两个工作项队列往往很有用。第一个队列用于所有从未尝试处理过的工作项。第二个队列是“重试”队列，用于任何已经至少有过一次（不成功的）处理尝试的消息。使用这种双队列方式，在上述局面下，重试队列里会堆积大量工作

— PDF 第 163 页 —

in the retry queue waiting for processing, but new work is no longer standing at the back of the line of retries. It has an equal chance of being processed along with the retry work. This two-queue approach is an example of a general priority queue approach, where different work queues have different priority and work is taken off the higher priority queue until it is empty, and then the next highest priority queue, etc. This can ensure that performance goes to where it is needed most to achieve latency goals.

等待处理，但新工作不再排在重试队列的队尾。它与重试工作被处理的概率是均等的。这种双队列方式是通用优先级队列方法的一个例子：不同工作队列有不同优先级，先从高优先级队列取工作直到它为空，然后再取下一个最高优先级队列，依此类推。这可以确保性能被投入到最需要的地方，以达成延迟目标。

Summary小结

This chapter has introduced the idea of a workflow. Workflows combine multiple work queues together into an orchestration of work to achieve some more complex objective. Multiple patterns for building workflows, from copying, to filtering, sharding, and merging were introduced. Finally, the important considerations of both performance and reliability in the face of slow work and worker crashes was examined. Using these patterns and error handling approaches, any complex work can be broken into an easily reasoned-about and constructed workflow for processing data reliably and efficiently.

本章引入了工作流的概念。工作流把多个工作队列组合成一种工作编排，以达成某个更复杂的目标。我们介绍了构建工作流的多种模式：从复制、过滤、分片到合并。最后，考察了在面对慢工作和 worker 崩溃时，性能与可靠性这两方面的重要考量。运用这些模式和错误处理方法，任何复杂的工作都可以被拆解成一个易于推理、易于构建的工作流，从而可靠而高效地处理数据。
